name: Meal Planner
description: The family's meals for every day of the week, a running-out guess for the things they buy from their order history, and a reminder each afternoon and evening with one cart per shopping app that is ordered only when they say yes; not for school runs, chores or appointments.

for: The family's meals for the week, planned every Sunday for every day of the week, each with its dishes
A guess of what is running out (atta, dal, oil) from the family's own order history on their shopping apps
A reminder at 3 pm and 7 pm with tonight's or tomorrow's meals, the items that may be running low and one cart per shopping app, ordered only when the family says yes
The family's saved recipes and each dish's video, planned into the week, and how each dish went last time
notFor: School runs, chores or appointments (use checklist or tracker)
Keeping a list of what is in the kitchen: it only guesses what is running out
A restaurant's menu or a business kitchen

setupOptions.about: Learn how this family eats and shops. Never brands, pack sizes or what's at home, or whether to add a regular. Nothing is ordered now. Each reply is read only into its facts; at the end the Meal Planner saves the whole setup itself from the household facts and the replies word for word (apply_setup), and its read-back is checked with the family.

routines.name: Weekly meal plan
routines.description: Every Sunday at 11, plans next week's meals, every day of it, in steps (the menu checked against every food rule, then each day's ingredients), saves the week, and asks the agent only to send the family the plan. It plans only: nothing is bought. On an install carried over from the old Meal Planner it first asks for the family's profile to be structured.

routines.name: Afternoon reminder
routines.description: Every day at 3 pm, when there is something to say: tonight's dinner, the ingredients to check, what you buy every day put on the cart as it comes due, and anything that may be running low. Nothing is ordered until you reply.

routines.name: Evening reminder
routines.description: Every day at 7 pm: reads new orders from your connected shopping apps, then tells you tomorrow's meals, puts what you buy every day on the cart as it comes due and asks about anything that may be running low. Nothing is ordered until you reply.

routines.name: Order clock
routines.description: Every 15 minutes: an order not paid within 24 hours is closed and its items go back on your cart (you are told once); an order stuck being placed for an hour goes back to your cart.

intents.name: sync-cart
intents.description: The family changed or opened their cart in Meal Planner: make the app's own cart match it.
intents.instructions: The payload has order_id, app and lines [{ item, product_id, name_on_app, qty }]. With that app's connector, make its cart hold exactly these lines (qty 0: take it off); touch only lines Meal Planner put there, and list any other line already in the cart as outside_lines. Read the cart back and call sync_cart { order_id, lines, total, delivery_gap, outside_lines }. A line the app does not have today (in_stock false): when the family has a fallback app (shopping.fallback in GET /api/family), take it off with set_cart_line { item, qty: 0, app } and move it with set_cart_line { item, qty, app: <fallback> }, then copy that cart to the fallback app and sync_cart it too; with no fallback, leave it marked. Send no message.

operations.description: The cook: who, which days, when they arrive, what they make well, what they do not make well or will not make, their time, and whether they try new recipes. { name, days?: ["Mon", ...], arrival?: "HH:MM" (a cook who comes more than once a day: a list of visits, ["06:00", "16:30"] or [{ at: "06:00", meals: ["Breakfast", "Lunch"] }, { at: "16:30", meals: ["Dinner"] }]; meals are slot names), makes_well?, wont_make?, time_limit?: in the family's words ("off to the next house at 9: a dish or two in the morning"), new_recipes?: open (tries recipes from reels and the internet) | set_menu (better with familiar dishes), note? }. name every time; days and arrival the first time. Only what you send changes; null clears a field. Plans never give the cook what is in wont_make, fit time_limit, and keep to familiar dishes with set_menu. A vague limit ("no fancy stuff") stays words only; ask "which dishes?" once when it matters.

operations.name: make_plan
operations.description: Plan some days, or a whole week, and save them, in one call: { from?: the first day as YYYY-MM-DD (today at the earliest), days?: how many days from it (1 to 14), keep_edited?: false to plan again the meals whose dishes the family set too (true when left out), week_start?: a week's Monday instead of from and days, household?: the household facts (Flock sends them; the app also reads them fresh), suggest_new?: true when the family said to suggest new dishes where it knows none of theirs (the setup's first week does this by itself) }. The setup's first plan is { from: today, days: 3 }; meals not said yet are lunch and dinner. The app plans it in steps itself (who eats each meal from the slots, the weekday patterns and the calendar; each meal slot from the family's own dishes and plates, checked against every food rule per person, how often each dish comes and no dish too soon again; then each day's ingredients), the same way the Sunday run does, and messages nobody. Answers { ok: true, message, intro?, instructions, defaults?, unmet? } (send message word for word, then intro once, as instructions say; defaults: what it assumed, to say once; unmet: what could not be kept, already said in message) or { ok: false, reason, say } (nothing planned: send say word for word; reason no_dishes: say is a question, the planner knows none of the family's dishes for some meals: add their answer with add_dish, then make_plan again, or make_plan with suggest_new: true when they say to suggest some).
operations.use: Plan some days or a week: the setup's first plan (3 days from today), the rest of the week after feedback, or "plan the next few days".

from.description: The first day to plan, YYYY-MM-DD (today at the earliest)

keep_edited.description: false: plan again the meals whose dishes the family set too

week_start.description: A whole week instead: its Monday, YYYY-MM-DD

suggest_new.description: Plan new dishes where the family named none of theirs

operations.name: set_slot
operations.description: Add, change or take away a meal slot for good (a child's tiffin, one person's own dinner, "Sunday lunch we eat out"). { name: the slot's name, kind?: main | custom | addon (needed for a new slot), addon_of?: the main slot an addon adds to, usual_people?: [names] ([] is everyone at home), days?: ["Mon", ...] ([] is every day), skip_days?: [{ day, skip: eaten_out | ordered_in }], order?: planning order (Breakfast 10, tiffin 20, Lunch 30, snacks 40, Dinner 50, add-ons 60), remove?: true }. The planned weeks' slot-days of that slot from today on are planned again (never one the family changed). Answers { ok, slot, replanned, message? } (send message word for word) or { ok, slot, planned: false, say }.
operations.use: A meal to plan for good: the main meals, a tiffin, one person's own plate, a meal always eaten out.

kind.description: main, custom (a tiffin, a snack) or addon (one person's own beside a main meal); needed for a new meal

addon_of.description: The main meal an addon adds to

usual_people.description: Who it is for ([] is everyone at home)

days.description: The days it is had ([] is every day)

skip_days.description: Weekdays it is eaten out or ordered in

order.description: Planning order: Breakfast 10, tiffin 20, Lunch 30, snacks 40, Dinner 50, add-ons 60

operations.name: set_slot_day
operations.description: A one-off change to one meal on one day: guests, someone away or joining, an occasion, eating out, or the dishes the family wants. { date, slot, people?: [names] (all of them), add_people?: [names] (a visitor too), remove_people?: [names], guests?: [{ count, rules?: [their food rules in words], as?: [names of the family they are, for a rule kept only when those people come] }], occasion?: in their words ("dinner party"), new_dishes_allowed?: how many new dishes that meal may have, skip?: eaten_out | ordered_in | null (cooked at home again), dishes?: [dish names] }. The meal is marked as the family's change and never planned over; its dishes are planned again for the change unless dishes are given or it is eaten out or ordered in. Answers { ok, slot_day, replanned, message?, proposed_rule? } (send message word for word) or { ok, slot_day, planned: false, say }. Dishes given in place of planned ones are kept as swaps; proposed_rule: a dish turned down twice, ask its say once and on a yes make its op call with its body.
operations.use: One meal on one day changes: guests, someone away or visiting, eating out, or the dishes they want instead.

as.description: The people of the family they are

new_dishes_allowed.description: How many new dishes that meal may have

skip.description: eaten_out, ordered_in, or null for cooked at home again

dishes.description: The dishes the family wants (a swap)

operations.name: add_dish
operations.description: Add a dish the family has to a slot's dishes, or one from a reel or recipe link they sent. { name, slot, frequency?: daily | usually | sometimes | rarely | "<n>/week", days?: ["Fri"] (only those days), quote?: their words, link?: the reel's or recipe's link }. What it contains is read before it answers. With link the dish is new to them: the link is its video, and the day after it is first planned the reminder asks whether they made and liked it. Answers { ok, dish }.
operations.use: The family named a dish they have (their usual plate, a favourite), or sent a reel for one to try.

slot.description: The meal it is had at

frequency.description: How often: daily, usually, sometimes, rarely, or "<n>/week"

link.description: A reel or recipe link for a dish new to them

operations.name: set_rule
operations.description: Add, change or take away a food rule (an allergy, no onion and garlic, millets twice a week for one person). { id?: the rule's id (to change or take away one; read the rules table), hard?: true for one always kept, what?: veg | egg | no_eggs | avoid | only | swap | require | fasting | cap | note, who?: a person (none: everyone), slots?: [slot names], days?: ["Mon", ...], items?: [tags, like "onion_garlic", "peanut", "white_rice"], to?: what a swap puts in place, frequency?: soft only, sometimes | usually | rarely | "<n>/week", per_meal?: dishes a meal (cap), fasting_food?: [what they eat when fasting], when_present?: [names]: the rule holds only at meals where one of them is (no eggs when the grandparents visit), quote?: the family's own words (needed for a new rule), remove?: true }. The planned meals from today on are checked again and only those that now fail are planned again. Answers { ok, rule, replanned, message? } (send message word for word) or { ok, rule, planned: false, say }.
operations.use: A food rule: a diet, an allergy, a fast or day rule, a rule for when someone visits, a wish ("millets twice a week").

id.description: The rule's id, to change or take one away

hard.description: true: always kept (diets, allergies, fasts); false: a wish kept some times a week

who.description: One person (none: everyone at the meal)

to.description: What a swap puts in place

frequency.description: Soft rules only: usually, sometimes, rarely, or "<n>/week"

when_present.description: Held only at meals where one of these people is (no eggs when the grandparents visit)

quote.description: Their own words (needed for a new rule)

operations.name: set_setting
operations.description: How many new dishes a week the plan may suggest. { new_dishes_per_week: 0 (none), 2 (1 to 2), 4 (3 to 4) or 7 (surprise me) }. Answers { ok, new_dishes_per_week }.
operations.use: The family said how many new dishes a week they want.

operations.name: record_made
operations.description: What the family says they made at a meal, when it was not the plan ("we made khichdi instead"). { date, slot, dishes: [dish names] }. The meal's dishes are replaced and kept as made. Only for today or before; a meal still to come is set_slot_day. Answers { ok, slot_day }.
operations.use: The family said they made something else ("we made khichdi instead"); never ask.

operations.name: record_feedback
operations.description: The answer to the reminder's question about a dish on yesterday's plan the family had not had before ("Did you make it, did you like it, and should I suggest it again?"). { date: the day it was planned, slot, dish: as the reminder named it, made: true or false, liked?: needed when made, again?: needed when made and liked; answer?: ok | swap | dont_like (in place of made, before a brand-new dish is cooked), who?: who said it, quote?: their words }. Made, liked and again: it becomes one of their dishes. Made and not liked: never planned again. Liked but not again: not planned again unless they ask. Not made: it may be planned once more. One call for each dish asked about; no reply, no call. The answer to a brand-new dish's "OK to try these, or should I swap any?" (the week's message) or "OK to make it, or swap?" (the evening before): ok: it becomes one of their dishes; swap: that day's meal is planned again with nothing new; dont_like: never suggested again, and a day still to come is planned again without it. Answers { ok, dish, outcome, replanned?, message?, proposed_rule? }: send message word for word when there is one; proposed_rule: a dish turned down twice, ask its say once and on a yes make its op call with its body.
operations.use: The answer about one planned dish: made and liked or not, or ok / swap / dont like before a new dish is cooked.

made.description: After the day: was it made

answer.description: Before a new dish is cooked: ok, swap, dont_like

operations.name: set_regular
operations.description: The older way to state an item's cycle, kept so earlier instructions still work; set_item is the one to use. { item, amount, unit, every: day | week | weekdays, times_per_week?, weekdays?: ["Mon", ...], for_whom?, active?, paused_until?: YYYY-MM-DD, remove?: true }. The same as set_item { item, usual_amount, unit, every_days }: amount with unit is what is bought each time; every with times_per_week or weekdays is how often (1 l every day; every: week with times_per_week: 2 is twice a week). It is kept on the item as its cycle and shown on the Pantry page; there is no separate list. paused_until snoozes the item up to and including that date; active: false or remove: true takes the stated cycle away; for_whom is not kept (an item has one cycle for the house). Answers { item }.
operations.use: Only for older instructions; use set_item.

weekdays.description: Weekdays: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

operations.name: import_order_history
operations.description: Give the app the family's past orders on one shopping app, one app a call; read them with that app's connector first (Amazon's cannot be read). { app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket | amazon (by id or name), account?: which of your accounts of this app, when you hold more than one (its account id, else its label; always the same one), orders: [{ date: YYYY-MM-DD, order_ref?: the app's order id, items: [{ item, group: daily | few_days | monthly (as set_item names them; send it with every item, so none is left to set one by one), product?, product_id?, pack?: "5 kg", pack_amount?, pack_unit?, count?, price?, image?: the product's picture link from the order's details }] }] }. item is the family's word for it (atta), product the name on the app, image the product's picture as the app's order details give it (Zepto's order detail, Instamart's order items), never one you made or searched for; count is how many packs (1 when left out). Send the oldest orders first, at most about 8 orders and 80 items a call, one app a call (a call carries 16 KB at most), and only the last 3 months: older orders are skipped, and so is an order dated after today. Send only delivered or paid orders, never a cancelled or failed one. Each item becomes a purchase; the same order sent again is recorded once, so a call may overlap the last. An item with its product_id is remembered as that app's product. More than one person may order for the house, each on their own account of the same app: each person's agent gives the orders of that person's account, and all of them count towards one cycle per item for the house. Holding more than one account of an app (Zepto (Arjun), Zepto (Meera)), read each and send each with its account: each has its own read_until, and an order with no order_ref is never taken for one of another account. The app works out each item's cycle (how much, how often) from the purchases by itself: ask the family to confirm nothing. Answers { recorded, duplicates, skipped_old, skipped_future, needs_group: [items to give a group with set_item], probably_out: [{ item, days_ago }], read_until: how far you have read this app, or this account of it (YYYY-MM-DD), said: what the house buys most often and how often, in a line ("milk (1 l every day), eggs (30 pc once a week)"), "" when nothing yet }.
operations.use: After reading one shopping app's past orders with its connector, one app a call.

app.description: A shopping app by id (or its name, like "Blinkit")

account.description: Which of your accounts of this app, when you hold more than one

orders.description: About 8 orders a call, oldest first, delivered or paid only

operations.name: record_bought_outside
operations.description: The family bought an item outside the apps ("got atta from the kirana"). { item, date?: YYYY-MM-DD, today when left out }. It counts as a purchase of the usual amount and restarts the item's estimate. Answers { event_id } or { duplicate: true }, and { item }.
operations.use: The family bought an item outside the apps ("got atta from the kirana").

operations.name: set_item
operations.description: Change one item the family buys, made when it is not there. { item, group?: daily | few_days | monthly (how often it is bought: daily every day or two, like milk; few_days within the week, like vegetables, eggs, bread; monthly lasts weeks, like atta, oil, masalas, cleaning and personal care), usual_amount?: what is bought each time, a number in unit, unit?: g | kg | ml | l | pc, every_days?: how many days one purchase lasts (1: every day; 7: once a week), follows_plan?: true when the week's meals use it up (paneer, rajma), dont_ask?: true to never ask about it or put it on the cart by itself, snooze_days?: days to leave it alone, for a holiday (null clears) }. usual_amount and every_days are the item's cycle as the family said it ("milk every day, 1 litre": { item: "milk", group: "daily", usual_amount: 1, unit: "l", every_days: 1 }; "a tray of 30 eggs once a week": usual_amount: 30, unit: "pc", every_days: 7): send them only when the family says so or there is no order history, since the app works the cycle out from the purchases and goes by those once they show one; null clears either. A daily item with a cycle goes on the cart by itself when it is due; the others are asked about. Only what you send changes. Answers { item }.
operations.use: The family said how much and how often they buy something, or not to ask about it.

usual_amount.description: What is bought each time, in unit

unit.description: g, kg, ml, l or pc

every_days.description: How many days one purchase lasts

follows_plan.description: The week's meals use it up

snooze_days.description: Days to leave it alone; null clears

operations.name: set_subscription
operations.description: An item delivered outside the apps (Country Delight, a milkman). { item, source: who delivers it, active: true | false }. active: true keeps it out of every cart and every question about running low, and takes it off the carts not yet ordered; active: false makes it an item like any other again. Answers { item }.
operations.use: An item comes from outside the apps (a milkman, Country Delight), or stops.

operations.name: answer_running_low
operations.description: The family's answers to "still in stock?". { answers: [{ item, answer: low | in_stock, days?: how many more days it will last }] }. low: it goes on the cart (answers { to_cart }). in_stock with days ("fine for a week": 7) is not asked again until then; in_stock without days ("still have it") waits a few days. Answers { to_cart: [items to add to the cart], items }.
operations.use: The family answered "still in stock?".

days.description: How many more days it lasts

operations.name: get_reminder
operations.description: The reminder to send now, built from the plan, the carts and what may be running low. { which: afternoon | evening, date?: the date the reminder's wake gave, YYYY-MM-DD (so a call after midnight builds that same reminder) }. afternoon is tonight's dinner, evening is tomorrow's meals; both put the daily items due tomorrow (by each item's cycle) on the cart and ask about at most 5 items that may be running low, each counted once per reminder however often you call it. Answers { which, date, meals, ask_ingredients, added, cart_items, asks: [{ item, days_ago }], delivery_gap, ordered: [{ order_id, app, message }], empty, text, app_text, block, carts: [{ order_id, app, status, lines, sync }] }. empty: send nothing. Send text on WhatsApp word for word, or app_text with block in the app chat. Read the connected apps' new orders into import_order_history before the first call. Copy each cart with sync: true to its app, then sync_cart, then call get_reminder again with the same which and date and send that answer. Check out every cart in ordered (Order without asking is on; a retry lists the same ones): say its message, check out, record_order.
operations.use: A reminder wake: build the reminder to send.

date.description: The date the reminder's wake gave

operations.name: get_cart
operations.description: The carts: one open cart per shopping app, and any being ordered. { app?: one app by id or name }. Answers { carts: [{ order_id, app, app_name, status: open | ordering, lines: [{ id, item, qty, product_id, name_on_app, pack, price, source, for_note }], total, delivery_gap, sync_state, synced_at, outside_lines, building_at_order }] }. A line at qty 0 is shown, not ordered.
operations.use: Read the carts before changing or ordering one.

operations.name: set_cart_line
operations.description: Put an item on the cart, change its qty or take it off. { item, qty: packs, a whole number (0 takes it off), app?: the app (else the one the family buys it on, else the main app), source?: added (default) | low | everyday | meal, for_note?, for_date?: YYYY-MM-DD, product_id?, name_on_app?, pack?, price?, image?: the product's picture link as the app gives it }. It goes on that app's open cart; while a cart is being ordered, a new item goes to a new open cart, and you may lower or take off a line of the cart being ordered ("remove the ghee"), and a higher qty or a new item goes to the open cart. An item delivered outside the apps is refused (code SUBSCRIPTION). Copy the change to the app's own cart yourself in the same turn, then sync_cart. Answers { line, cart }.
operations.use: Put an item on a cart, change its qty or take it off ("add dal").

app.description: A shopping app by id (or its name, like "Blinkit")

operations.name: order_cart
operations.description: The family said yes to ordering one app's cart (a reply, or the message "Order my <App> cart" from the Order button). { app }. The cart is being ordered from now on, and anything added later goes to a new cart. Send its message word for word, check out on the app, then record_order. Asked again while that order is being placed, it answers the same order. Answers { order_id, app, lines, message }; an empty cart is refused (409).
operations.use: The family said yes to ordering one app's cart.

app.description: A shopping app by id (or its name, like "Blinkit")

operations.name: sync_cart
operations.description: What the app's own cart holds after you copied a cart to it, or read it back. { order_id, lines: [{ product_id, qty, price?, in_stock?: false when the app does not have it today }], total?: the app's cart total, delivery_gap?: rupees short of free delivery, outside_lines?: [{ name, qty? }] (lines in the app's cart Meal Planner did not put there) }. Answers { cart }.
operations.use: After copying a cart to its app, or reading the app's cart back.

operations.name: record_order
operations.description: What happened to an order being placed. { order_id, placed?: true, paid?: true | false, app_order_ref?: the app's order id, total? }. placed: its lines become purchases and the items' estimates restart. paid: false (not paid): the purchases stop counting and the lines go back on the open cart; paid: true later brings both back. When you record paid: false, tell the family yourself: the clock will not. Send app_order_ref whenever you have it, also later. Answers { order }, and taken_off: [{ order_id, items }] when a late payment took returned items off a cart being ordered: take them off that checkout on the app too.
operations.use: An order was placed, paid, or not paid.

operations.name: cancel_order
operations.description: Stop an order. { order_id }. One being ordered goes back to the open cart (nothing was placed); a placed one counts as not paid, its lines back on the cart, and you tell the family so yourself: the clock will not. Answers { order }.
operations.use: Stop an order being placed, or let a placed one go.

operations.name: remember_product
operations.description: Remember the product an item is bought as on a grocery app, so the next order reuses it without searching. { item, app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket, product_id, name_on_app, pack?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }. item is the family's word for it, exactly as on the order line or the pantry item (milk), never the product's name on the app; pack_amount and pack_unit are the pack's size as a number and its measure (500, ml), which the app counts packs with (a plain pack text like "500 ml" is read too). One product per item and app: sending it again takes the place of the one remembered. Answers { product }.
operations.use: You picked the product an item is bought as on an app.

app.description: A shopping app by id (or its name, like "Blinkit")

operations.name: save_recipe
operations.description: Save a recipe, or change one. { recipe_id?, name?, links?: [the reel, short or page], notes?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], tags?: ["breakfast", "tiffin"], for?: [names], thumbnail? }. Without recipe_id, a recipe that already holds one of the links is the one changed (new links are added to it), so a link shared twice is saved once; otherwise a new recipe is made, and it needs a name: with none the answer is code NEEDS_NAME, so ask the family what to call it and save again. By recipe_id only what you send changes, and links you send replace its links. Answers { recipe }.
operations.use: The family shared a reel or recipe and said "save this".

operations.name: set_dish_video
operations.description: Give a dish its one video, or take it away. { dish: its name as planned, or dish_id, url: the link (a YouTube video, an Instagram reel, any page; never a file), title?, thumbnail?: the video's picture link, remove?: true }. The video is the dish's, kept by its name: every week the dish is planned it shows on the Week page and in the cook's message, with no call again. Find one with your own search when the family asks ("find a video for rajma"); a recipe or reel the family shares for a dish is its video too. A YouTube link's thumbnail is filled in when you send none. A second video takes the place of the first. Answers { dish: { name, video, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history } }.
operations.use: Give a dish its video ("find a video for rajma").

operations.name: rate_dishes
operations.description: How dishes went when the family ate them. { date?: the day they were eaten, today when left out, ratings: [{ dish: its name as planned, or dish_id, rating: good | okay | didnt_work, note?: what went well or didn't, in their words ("too oily"), said_by?: who said it, again?: false to never plan it again }] }. One call for all of a reply. The latest rating and its note show the next time the dish is planned ("last time: too oily") on the Week page and in the cook's message; a short history is kept. A dish rated didnt_work is planned rarely, not never; again: false never. Answers { dishes: [{ name, video, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history }], proposed_rule? } (a dish turned down twice: ask its say once and on a yes make its op call with its body).
operations.use: The family said how dishes went ("the dal was too salty").

date.description: The day they were eaten, today when left out

note.description: What went well or not, in their words

operations.name: get_dish
operations.description: What the app knows of one dish. { dish: its name as planned }. Answers { dish: { name, video: { url, title, thumbnail } or null, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history: [{ rating, note, date, by }] } }, empty for a dish it knows nothing of.
operations.use: Read one dish's video and how it went last time.

agentInterface.instructions: Meal Planner owns this family's people, meals, the items they buy, their carts and recipes. Read the app before you answer and change it only through its operations, then tell the family what the app now says. A routine wake (the Sunday plan, the 15:00 and 19:00 reminders) names its own steps. What the app writes for the family (a plan's message and intro, a reminder's text, an order's message) is sent word for word. Nothing is ordered until the family replies or taps Order: "Order my <App> cart" is that yes. Setting up: follow the planner-setup skill and status. Call guide when unsure which operation fits. Save the family's own words; never fill anything from guesses. A shared reel plus "save this" is a save_recipe call; for a dish it is also its video (set_dish_video). How a meal went is rate_dishes.

publishedSkills.name: Setting up meals
publishedSkills.description: How to set up Meal Planner with a family in chat: the two grouped questions, saving each fact with the right operation, the first 3-day plan, the feedback round and the rest of the week.
